Scenario: INITIAL_DIAGNOSIS
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED

Scenario: INITIAL_DIAGNOSIS

patient_vignette: A 29-year-old man with exertional dyspnea is evaluated for possible hereditary cardiomyopathy after echocardiography shows mild asymmetric septal hypertrophy. A panel identifies a heterozygous missense variant in a gene known to cause hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, and the laboratory notes that his phenotype falls within the recognized spectrum for that gene. The variant is also present in a public database with several submissions, but the report states that the entries come from a manually curated source with clearly described methods, the nomenclature is HGVS-compliant, and the genome build and transcript are specified. On closer review, however, the database frequency is low and not obviously higher than expected for the disorder, and the submitter descriptions do not indicate whether the observations were independent. The cardiologist asks whether the phenotype match and database presence are enough to call the variant pathogenic or benign.

rules_text:
Rule ID: R001
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: all patients with endometrial cancer after potentially curative primary treatment and no evidence of disease
Guideline Action: counsel about potential symptoms of recurrence
Source Statement: It is recommended that all patients receive counselling about the potential symptoms of recurrence of endometrial cancer, because the majority of recurrences in the identified studies were symptomatic.

Rule ID: R002
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: patient is surgically or pathologically confirmed low risk of recurrence (stage IA or IB, grade 1 or 2)
Guideline Action: perform general examination including complete history and pelvic-rectal examination semi-annually or annually for the first 3 years, then annually for the next 2 years
Source Statement: For patients at a surgically or pathologically confirmed low risk of recurrence (i.e., stage IA or IB, grade 1 or 2): A general examination, including a complete history and a pelvicrectal examination, conducted semi-annually or annually for the first three years and annually for the next two years.

Rule ID: R003
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: patient is high risk of recurrence (stage IA or IB, grade 3, or stage IC or advanced stage)
Guideline Action: perform general examination including complete history and pelvic-rectal examination every 3 to 6 months for the first 3 years, then semi-annually for the next 2 years
Source Statement: For patients at high risk of recurrence (i.e., stage IA or IB, grade 3, or stage IC or advanced stage). A general examination, including a complete history and a pelvic-rectal examination, every three to six months for the first three years and semi-annually for the next two years.

Rule ID: R004
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: planning follow-up setting or specialist type for any patient
Guideline Action: follow the patient with a health care professional knowledgeable about the natural history of the disease and comfortable performing speculum and pelvic exams
Source Statement: There is insufficient evidence to inform the optimum clinical setting or type of specialist required for follow-up; however, it is recommended that all patients be followed by a health care professional who is knowledgeable about the natural history of the disease, and who is comfortable performing speculum and pelvic exams, in order to diagnose or detect a local (vaginal) recurrence.

Rule ID: R005
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: patient has symptoms suggestive of recurrence
Guideline Action: perform targeted investigation to rule out recurrence
Source Statement: It is recommended that all patients undergo a targeted investigation to rule out recurrence if symptomatic, since patients with local recurrence are potentially curable with further therapy.

Rule ID: R006
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: treatment includes radiotherapy
Guideline Action: counsel the patient on potential adverse effects of radiotherapy
Source Statement: Where treatment with radiotherapy is involved, it is recommended that patients be counselled on the potential adverse effects of radiotherapy.

Rule ID: R007
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 60
Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER
Activation Condition: all patients with endometrial cancer after potentially curative primary treatment and no evidence of disease
Guideline Action: use a follow-up strategy based on recurrence risk and patient preferences
Source Statement: The most appropriate follow-up strategy is likely one based upon the risk of recurrence, with individual patient preferences for more or less follow-up taken into account.

Rule ID: R008
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 60
Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER
Activation Condition: patient has remained recurrence-free for 5 years
Guideline Action: return to annual population-based general physical and pelvic examination
Source Statement: Since the majority of patients with recurrence were symptomatic and virtually all recurred within five years, it seems reasonable that patients return to annual population-based general physical and pelvic examination after five years of recurrence-free follow-up.

patient_vignette: A 62-year-old man is diagnosed with stage III squamous cell carcinoma of the oropharynx after biopsy of a persistent throat lesion and CT imaging showing a primary tumor with suspicious cervical nodes. He is referred to a multidisciplinary head and neck cancer clinic where the medical oncologist, radiation oncologist, head and neck surgeon, speech-language pathologist, dietitian, and social worker review his case together. The team discusses definitive treatment planning, swallowing rehabilitation, nutritional support, and survivorship needs. His family physician is informed of the diagnosis and remains responsible for his general medical care and supportive follow-up after cancer treatment. Because he may need surgery depending on response to therapy, the surgeon notes that reconstruction expertise would be required if an operation becomes necessary.

His urologist notes that he is at elevated risk for clinically significant prostate cancer and is considering imaging before biopsy. The patient is willing to undergo testing only if it would directly change management, but he is not interested in curative therapy.
rules_text:
Rule ID: R001
Scenario: INITIAL_DIAGNOSIS
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: Biopsy-naive patient at elevated risk of clinically significant prostate cancer and a candidate for curative management with suspected clinically localized prostate cancer
Guideline Action: Perform multiparametric MRI prior to biopsy
Source Statement: MPMRI is recommended prior to biopsy in patients who are candidates for curative management with suspected clinically localized prostate cancer.

Rule ID: R002
Scenario: INITIAL_DIAGNOSIS
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: Biopsy-naive patient has a positive multiparametric MRI
Guideline Action: Perform multiparametric MRI-targeted biopsy together with transrectal ultrasound systematic biopsy
Source Statement: If the MPMRI is positive, MPMRI-TB and TRUS-SB should be performed together to maximize detection of CSPCa.

Rule ID: R003
Scenario: RECURRENCE_OR_RESTAGING
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: Patient had a prior negative transrectal ultrasound systematic biopsy and is at high risk of clinically significant prostate cancer with curative management being considered
Guideline Action: Perform multiparametric MRI
Source Statement: In patients who had a prior negative TRUS-SB and demonstrate a high risk of having CSPCa in whom curative management is being considered: MPMRI should be performed,

Rule ID: R004
Scenario: RECURRENCE_OR_RESTAGING
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: Patient had a prior negative transrectal ultrasound systematic biopsy and multiparametric MRI is positive
Guideline Action: Perform targeted biopsy
Source Statement: If the MPMRI is positive, targeted biopsy should be performed.

Rule ID: R005
Scenario: INITIAL_DIAGNOSIS
Priority: 60
Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER
Activation Condition: Biopsy-naive patient has a negative multiparametric MRI
Guideline Action: Consider forgoing biopsy after discussing risks and benefits with the patient and arranging ongoing follow-up
Source Statement: If the MPMRI is negative, consider forgoing any biopsy after discussion of the risks and benefits with the patient as part of shared decision making and ongoing followup.

Rule ID: R006
Scenario: INITIAL_DIAGNOSIS
Priority: 60
Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER
Activation Condition: Biopsy-naive patient has a negative multiparametric MRI
Guideline Action: Inform the patient that a negative multiparametric MRI may miss clinically significant prostate cancer
Source Statement: Between 8% and 24% of patients with CSPCa may be missed by a negative MPMRI.

Rule ID: R007
Scenario: INITIAL_DIAGNOSIS
Priority: 60
Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER
Activation Condition: Considering multiparametric MRI for a biopsy-naive patient
Guideline Action: Use multiparametric MRI only if high-quality interpretation is available and operators have experience performing targeted biopsies
Source Statement: MPMRI should only be performed if there is availability of high-quality MPMRI interpretation and operators with experience performing targeted biopsies (see Recommendation 3).

Rule ID: R008
Scenario: INITIAL_DIAGNOSIS
Priority: 60
Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER
Activation Condition: Considering multiparametric MRI for a biopsy-naive patient
Guideline Action: Use multiparametric MRI only when there is intent for curative management if biopsy is positive
Source Statement: Due to the limited availability, MPMRI is recommended only for patients where there is intent of curative management should the biopsy be positive for CSPCa.

rules_text:
Rule ID: R001
Scenario: TREATMENT_RESPONSE
Priority: 80
Recommendation Class: NOT_RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: platinum-resistant recurrent ovarian cancer and not eligible for the AURELIA trial criteria
Guideline Action: Do not apply the bevacizumab plus chemotherapy option described for AURELIA-eligible patients.
Source Statement: Ineligible patients include those who have received >2 prior anticancer regimens or who had refractory disease, patients with a history of bowel obstruction (including subocclusive disease) related to underlying disease, a history of abdominal fistula, gastrointestinal perforation, or intra-abdominal abscess, or evidence of rectosigmoid involvement by pelvic examination, bowel involvement on computed tomography, or clinical symptoms of bowel obstruction.

Rule ID: R002
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: all patients with recurrent epithelial ovarian cancer
Guideline Action: Assess each patient individually for recurrence status, platinum sensitivity, toxicity, ease of administration, and patient preference; recognize systemic therapy is not curative.
Source Statement: Systemic therapy for recurrent ovarian cancer is not curative. As such, it is recognized that, to determine the optimal therapy, each patient needs to be assessed individually in terms of recurrence, sensitivity to platinum, toxicity, ease of administration, and patient preference.

Rule ID: R003
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: all patients with recurrent epithelial ovarian cancer
Guideline Action: Offer participation in clinical trials if appropriate.
Source Statement: All patients should be offered the opportunity to participate in clinical trials, if appropriate.

Rule ID: R004
Scenario: TREATMENT_RESPONSE
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: platinum-sensitive recurrent ovarian cancer and a single platinum agent is not being considered because of toxicity or allergy
Guideline Action: Use monotherapy with paclitaxel, topotecan, or pegylated liposomal doxorubicin.
Source Statement: If a single platinum agent is not being considered (e.g., because of toxicity or allergy), then monotherapy with paclitaxel, topotecan, or pegylated liposomal doxorubicin is a reasonable treatment option.

Rule ID: R005
Scenario: TREATMENT_RESPONSE
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: platinum-sensitive recurrent ovarian cancer with known BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation, somatic or germline, after platinum-based chemotherapy for recurrent disease
Guideline Action: Use PARP inhibitor maintenance treatment post platinum-based chemotherapy.
Source Statement: PARP inhibitors are recommended for patients with known BRCA 1 or 2 mutation (somatic and germline) as maintenance treatment post platinum-based chemotherapy for recurrent disease.

Rule ID: R006
Scenario: TREATMENT_RESPONSE
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: platinum-refractory or platinum-resistant recurrent ovarian cancer

Source Statement: Lower levels of response to treatment are expected for this group; therefore, the goals of treatment should be to improve patient's quality of life by extending the symptom-free interval, reducing symptom intensity, increasing progression-free interval, or if possible, prolonging life.

Priority: 70

Source Statement: Single-agent paclitaxel, topotecan, pegylated liposomal doxorubicin, and gemcitabine have demonstrated activity in this patient population and are reasonable treatment options.

patient_vignette: A 34-year-old elementary school teacher comes to urgent care after hearing that several students in her district developed sudden vomiting and diarrhea within the same day. She is visibly anxious and says parents are “panicking” on social media, asking whether the school cafeteria food was contaminated and whether this could be a deliberate poisoning. The clinic has not yet received confirmed public health information, and local officials are still investigating the source and scope of the illness.

Rule ID: R001
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 80
Recommendation Class: NOT_RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: When the public may be worried or outraged
Guideline Action: Do not dismiss outrage or tell people they should not be afraid.
Source Statement: Don't Dismiss Outrage. ... When people are afraid and worried, the worst thing to do is pretend that they're not. The second worst thing is to tell them they shouldn't be.

Rule ID: R002
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 80
Recommendation Class: NOT_RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: When giving reassurance during an early crisis
Guideline Action: Do not over-reassure or minimize the risk.
Source Statement: Don't over-reassure. ... Reassurance can backfire.

Rule ID: R003
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 80
Recommendation Class: NOT_RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: When the public or media ask about cause, blame, or liability early in the event
Guideline Action: Do not discuss liability, blame, or cause before the situation is contained.
Source Statement: Avoid discussing liability: Questions of cause, blame, responsibility, and liability often follow a crisis. It is not appropriate to discuss them at the early stages.

Rule ID: R004
Scenario: GENERAL

He had been stacking boxes and moving pallets for about 90 minutes with only brief water breaks. On the site nurse’s check, his oral temperature is 38.4°C, and he reports marked fatigue, heavy sweating, and a throbbing headache. rules_text:
Rule ID: R001
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 80
Recommendation Class: NOT_RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: heat exposure is prolonged or severe enough to cause body temperature above 38°C
Guideline Action: do not continue further exposures during the same day
Source Statement: There is abundant evidence that the physiological strain of an exposure which raises body temperature above 38°C is such as to contraindicate further exposures during the same day; it may take hours for complete recovery.

Rule ID: R002
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: employee exposure to heat in the workplace
Guideline Action: control heat exposure by requiring compliance with the work practice standard
Source Statement: NIOSH recommends that employee exposure to heat in the workplace be controlled by requiring compliance with the work practice standard set forth in the following sections.

Rule ID: R003
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: hot environmental conditions exceed WBGT 79°F
Guideline Action: apply the standard to all places of employment indoors and outdoors and to all employees except those required to wear impermeable protective clothing
Source Statement: The provisions of this standard are applicable to all places of employment, indoors and outdoors, and to all employees except those who are required to wear impermeable protective clothing.

Rule ID: R004
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: continuous exposure for one hour or intermittent exposure for two hours and WBGT exceeds 79°F for men or 76°F for women
Guideline Action: initiate one or a combination of the listed protective practices to keep body core temperature from exceeding 100.4°F
Source Statement: When exposure of an employee is continuous for one hour or intermittent for a period of two hours and the time-weighted average WBGT exceeds 79°F for men or 76°F for women, then any one or combination of the following practices shall be initiated to insure that the employee's body care temperature does not exceed 100.4°F:

Rule ID: R005
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: employee is unacclimatized
Guideline Action: acclimatize over 6 days starting at 50 percent of anticipated total work load and time exposure on day 1, then increase by 10 percent daily to 100 percent on day 6
Source Statement: Unacclimatized employees shall be acclimatized over a period of 6 days. The acclimatization schedule shall begin with 50 percent of the anticipated total work load and time exposure on the first day, followed by daily 10 percent increments building up 100 percent total exposure on the sixth day.

Rule ID: R006
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: regular acclimatized employee returns after nine or more consecutive calendar days of leave
Guideline Action: use a 4-day reacclimatization schedule starting at 50 percent on day 1 and increasing by 20 percent daily to 100 percent on day 4
Source Statement: Regular acclimatized employees who return from nine or more consecutive calendar days of leave, shall undergo a four day acclimatization period. The acclimatization schedule shall begin with 50 percent of the anticipated total exposure on the first day, followed by daily 20 percent increments building up to 100 percent total exposure on the fourth day.

Rule ID: R007
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: regular acclimatized employee returns after four consecutive days of illness
Guideline Action: obtain medical permission to return to work and use a 4-day reacclimatization schedule as above
Source Statement: Regular acclimatized employees who return from four consecutive days of illness should have medical permission to return to the job, and should undergo a four day re-acclimatization period as defined in (2) above.

Rule ID: R008
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: workers are exposed to hot jobs
Guideline Action: implement a work and rest regimen to reduce peaks of physiological strain and improve recovery during rest periods
Source Statement: A work and rest regimen shall be implemented to reduce the peaks of physiological strain and to improve recovery during rest periods.

Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70

Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70

Priority: 70

Source Statement: All susceptible persons traveling to or working in countries that have high or intermediate hepatitis A endemicity (Figure 4) should be vaccinated or receive IG before departure (Tables 1-4). Hepatitis A vaccination at the age-appropriate dose is preferred (Tables 2-4).

He notes that he will only be staying at a resort in Lima and on the Pacific coast, with no plans to visit rural areas, eat street food, or travel outside the capital region. Because departure is soon, he would like protection as quickly as possible and is willing to be vaccinated today.
rules_text:
Rule ID: R001
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: routine prevention of hepatitis A in the United States
Guideline Action: Implement routine hepatitis A vaccination for children nationwide.
Source Statement: All children should receive hepatitis A vaccine at age 1 year (i.e., 12-23 months).

Rule ID: R002
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: state, county, or community already has a hepatitis A vaccination program for children aged 2-18 years
Guideline Action: Maintain the existing childhood hepatitis A vaccination program.
Source Statement: States, counties, and communities with existing hepatitis A vaccination programs for children aged 2-18 years are encouraged to maintain these programs.

Rule ID: R003
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: person is traveling to or working in a country with high or intermediate hepatitis A endemicity and is susceptible
Guideline Action: Vaccinate before departure or give immune globulin before departure; vaccine is preferred.
Source Statement: All susceptible persons traveling to or working in countries that have high or intermediate hepatitis A endemicity (Figure 4) should be vaccinated or receive IG before departure (Tables 1-4). Hepatitis A vaccination at the age-appropriate dose is preferred (Tables 2-4).

Rule ID: R004
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: travel is planned and first vaccine dose can be given now
Guideline Action: Give the first hepatitis A vaccine dose as soon as travel is considered.
Source Statement: The first dose of hepatitis A vaccine should be administered as soon as travel is considered.

Rule ID: R005
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: traveler departs in less than 4 weeks and cannot or will not receive immune globulin
Guideline Action: Still give hepatitis A vaccine and inform the traveler protection may be incomplete for the next 2-4 weeks.
Source Statement: Travelers departing in <4 weeks who do not or cannot receive IG should nonetheless receive hepatitis A vaccine and be informed that they might not be optimally protected from acquiring hepatitis A in the immediate future (i.e., subsequent 2-4 weeks).

Rule ID: R006
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: traveler is allergic to a vaccine component or declines vaccine
Guideline Action: Give a single dose of immune globulin 0.02 mL/kg; if travel lasts more than 2 months, use 0.06 mL/kg and repeat if travel lasts more than 5 months.
Source Statement: Travelers who are allergic to a vaccine component or who elect not to receive vaccine should receive a single dose of IG (0.02 mL/kg), which provides effective protection against hepatitis A for up to 3 months (Table 1). Travelers whose travel period is >2 months should be administered IG at 0.06 mL/kg; administration must be repeated if the travel period is >5 months (Table 1).

Rule ID: R007
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: person is an adolescent or adult man who has sex with men
Guideline Action: Vaccinate against hepatitis A.
Source Statement: MSM (both adolescents and adults) should be vaccinated.

Rule ID: R008
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: person uses injection or noninjection illicit drugs
Guideline Action: Vaccinate against hepatitis A.
Source Statement: Vaccination is recommended for users of injection and noninjection illicit drugs.

patient_vignette: A 15-year-old student is brought to a school health planning meeting after the district notices inconsistent food practices across campuses. The middle school is drafting a new nutrition policy because vending machines, classroom celebrations, and fundraisers currently vary by teacher and club. Parents have asked for healthier options, while students want foods that fit cultural preferences and after-school sports schedules. The school nurse reports that some teachers use candy as rewards, and the PTA is considering a fundraiser built around soda and chips. Administrators want a policy that can be rolled out this semester but also updated after feedback from families, staff, and students. The team is looking for a practical plan that supports healthy eating without ignoring local food traditions or the needs of different student groups.

Scenario: GENERAL

Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70

Guideline Action: Consider alemtuzumab
Source Statement: the UK CLL Forum guideline recommended alemtuzumab for use in patients without bulky lymphadenopathy (<5cm), who were previously treated with alkylating agents and refractory to fludarabine.

Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 60

He reports increasing fatigue, dyspnea on exertion, poor appetite, and intermittent anxiety about his family’s future. His wife says he has become more withdrawn and is struggling to talk about goals of care. He is not in the final days of life, but his symptoms are worsening and he asks for help managing them at home while continuing cancer-directed therapy. The oncology team notes that his physical symptoms are only part of the problem; he also needs emotional support and help for his wife, who is overwhelmed by caregiving responsibilities.

Rule ID: R001
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: When providing palliative care across the disease course
Guideline Action: Use a team-based approach that addresses both physical and non-physical symptoms and supports patients and families.
Source Statement: Palliative care focuses on care that addresses both physical and non-physical symptoms; it can be delivered throughout the course of the disease; it involves a team of healthcare providers and supports patients as well as their families.

Rule ID: R002
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: When selecting palliative care guidelines for review
Guideline Action: Include only papers that provide recommendations on palliative care and exclude papers that only describe guideline or consensus methods without recommendations.
Source Statement: Papers were included if they provided any recommendations on palliative care. Papers were excluded if they only provided guideline or consensus methods and no recommendations.

Rule ID: R003
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: When screening palliative care guidelines for this review
Guideline Action: Restrict inclusion to guidelines published from 2011 to 2016.
Source Statement: Due to the large number of guidelines, the Working Group decided to restrict the review to include only guidelines published in the past five years (2011 to 2016).

Rule ID: R004
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: When selecting higher-quality guidelines for this review
Guideline Action: Include only guidelines with an AGREE Rigour of Development subsection score of 28 or higher.
Source Statement: To identify the best-quality guidelines, the AGREE Instrument Rigour of Development scale was used and only guidelines that scored 28 or above were included in this review.

Rule ID: R005
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: When using the broad palliative care guideline for adults
Guideline Action: Apply the guideline covering the palliative care path from first diagnosis of serious illness to death.
Source Statement: The "Palliative Care for Adults" guideline by McCusker et al. ... covers the palliative care path from the patient's first diagnosis of a serious illness to death.

Rule ID: R006
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: When caring for patients in the last days and hours of life
Guideline Action: Use the Registered Nurses Association of Ontario guideline for nurse-specific recommendations on assessment, decision support, care and management, education, and organization/policy.
Source Statement: This is a Canadian guideline about patient care in the last days and hours of life, and the recommendations in this guideline were specific to nurses. The guideline makes recommendations in the following areas: Assessment for end of life, Decision support at end of life, Care and management at end of life, Education, and Organization and policy recommendations.

Rule ID: R007
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: When assessing or preventing pressure ulcers in palliative care
Guideline Action: Use the Registered Nurses Association of Ontario guideline for nurse-specific recommendations on assessment, planning, interventions, discharge or transfer/care arrangements, and education/organization-policy.
Source Statement: The topic of this guideline was the assessment and prevention of pressure ulcers. This guideline does not focus solely on palliative care, but the treatment and assessment of pressure ulcers in palliative care is a part of the guideline. ... The guideline makes recommendations in the following areas: Assessment, Planning, Interventions, Discharge or transfer or the care arrangements, and Education and organization/policy.

patient_vignette: A 68-year-old man with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer was diagnosed 9 months ago and is now on second-line treatment after progression. He reports increasing fatigue, dyspnea on exertion, poor appetite, and intermittent anxiety about his family’s future. His wife says he has become more withdrawn and is struggling to talk about goals of care. He is not in the final days of life, but his symptoms are worsening and he asks for help managing them at home while continuing cancer-directed therapy. The oncology team notes that his physical symptoms are only part of the problem; he also needs emotional support and help for his wife, who is overwhelmed by caregiving responsibilities. His last hospitalization ended with a do-not-resuscitate order, but he and his oncologist still expect active disease-directed treatment and do not consider him to be in the terminal phase.

At his oncology follow-up, he asks whether he should start imatinib to reduce the chance of recurrence. He has no evidence of residual or metastatic disease on postoperative imaging, and the tumor was completely removed. He feels well and is eager to do anything that might lower recurrence risk, but he has not started any systemic therapy yet.

patient_vignette: A 58-year-old man with primary systemic AL amyloidosis presents after 5 months of bortezomib-based therapy with partial hematologic response. He has persistent nephrotic-range proteinuria and mild peripheral edema, but no symptomatic heart failure. Echocardiography shows preserved ejection fraction with mild concentric thickening, and his creatinine is stable at 1.1 mg/dL. His hematologist discusses stem cell transplantation as a next step. Because he has AL amyloidosis and is being evaluated for SCT, the team reviews his organ involvement, overall functional status, comorbidities, and treatment goals before deciding whether he is an appropriate transplant candidate.

patient_vignette: A 67-year-old man presents with a PSA of 11.8 ng/mL and an abnormal digital rectal exam showing mild left-sided induration. He has never had a prostate biopsy. He is otherwise healthy, has a life expectancy well beyond 10 years, and says he would want curative treatment if clinically significant prostate cancer is found. His urologist considers him at elevated risk for clinically significant, clinically localized prostate cancer and is planning diagnostic workup before biopsy. Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 60
Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER

Guideline Action: Consider second-line chemotherapy only after weighing treatment-free interval, response to first-line therapy, residual toxicity, and performance status.

Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 60
Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER
Activation Condition: patient relapses three or more months after completion of first-line chemotherapy
Guideline Action: Consider retreatment with the same regimen that produced the initial response, generally etoposide-cisplatin.
Source Statement: patients who relapse three or more months following the completion of first-line chemotherapy may benefit from retreatment with the same regimen that induced their initial response. This would generally mean retreatment with etoposide-cisplatin.

The patient says he wants care that fits his priorities—staying alert enough to talk with family and avoiding prolonged ICU treatment if recovery is unlikely—but he has not had a structured conversation about these values. The team is considering a new outpatient ACP workflow and realizes that a few isolated steps have not changed care quality in the past.

patient_vignette: A 68-year-old man with metastatic lung cancer is admitted for progressive dyspnea and fatigue. His oncology team notes that advance care planning has been discussed inconsistently across visits: one clinician focused mainly on code status, while another gave a pamphlet about end-of-life decisions. The patient says he wants care that fits his priorities—staying alert enough to talk with family and avoiding prolonged ICU treatment if recovery is unlikely—but he has not had a structured conversation about these values. His daughter asks whether these discussions might upset him, since he becomes anxious when illness is mentioned. The team is planning a brief clinician-education session on ACP, but there is no broader workflow redesign, standardized documentation, or interprofessional process in place.

Rule ID: R001
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 80
Recommendation Class: NOT_RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: When considering limited ACP implementation
Guideline Action: Do not rely on only one or a few ACP elements to achieve meaningful patient care impact.
Source Statement: Addressing only one, or a few, of these elements creates the risks of leaving critical gaps that could prevent positive impacts on quality patient care.

Rule ID: R002
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 80
Recommendation Class: NOT_RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: When using education alone to improve ACP care
Guideline Action: Do not expect education alone to improve care or patient experience without supporting system changes.
Source Statement: However, high-quality education, although essential, on its own is unlikely to improve care or the patient experience in the absence of supporting systemic changes.

Rule ID: R003
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 80

Guideline Action: Do not assume ACP discussions increase distress in children or parents.

Priority: 60

rules_text:
Rule ID: R001
Scenario: TREATMENT_RESPONSE
Priority: 80
Recommendation Class: NOT_RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: platinum-resistant recurrent ovarian cancer and not eligible for the AURELIA trial criteria
Guideline Action: Do not apply the bevacizumab plus chemotherapy option described for AURELIA-eligible patients.
Source Statement: Ineligible patients include those who have received >2 prior anticancer regimens or who had refractory disease, patients with a history of bowel obstruction (including subocclusive disease) related to underlying disease, a history of abdominal fistula, gastrointestinal perforation, or intra-abdominal abscess, or evidence of rectosigmoid involvement by pelvic examination, bowel involvement on computed tomography, or clinical symptoms of bowel obstruction.

Rule ID: R002
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: all patients with recurrent epithelial ovarian cancer
Guideline Action: Assess each patient individually for recurrence status, platinum sensitivity, toxicity, ease of administration, and patient preference; recognize systemic therapy is not curative.
Source Statement: Systemic therapy for recurrent ovarian cancer is not curative. As such, it is recognized that, to determine the optimal therapy, each patient needs to be assessed individually in terms of recurrence, sensitivity to platinum, toxicity, ease of administration, and patient preference.

Rule ID: R003
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: all patients with recurrent epithelial ovarian cancer
Guideline Action: Offer participation in clinical trials if appropriate.
Source Statement: All patients should be offered the opportunity to participate in clinical trials, if appropriate.

Rule ID: R004
Scenario: TREATMENT_RESPONSE
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: platinum-sensitive recurrent ovarian cancer and a single platinum agent is not being considered because of toxicity or allergy
Guideline Action: Use monotherapy with paclitaxel, topotecan, or pegylated liposomal doxorubicin.
Source Statement: If a single platinum agent is not being considered (e.g., because of toxicity or allergy), then monotherapy with paclitaxel, topotecan, or pegylated liposomal doxorubicin is a reasonable treatment option.

Rule ID: R005
Scenario: TREATMENT_RESPONSE
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: platinum-sensitive recurrent ovarian cancer with known BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation, somatic or germline, after platinum-based chemotherapy for recurrent disease
Guideline Action: Use PARP inhibitor maintenance treatment post platinum-based chemotherapy.
Source Statement: PARP inhibitors are recommended for patients with known BRCA 1 or 2 mutation (somatic and germline) as maintenance treatment post platinum-based chemotherapy for recurrent disease.

Rule ID: R006
Scenario: TREATMENT_RESPONSE
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: platinum-refractory or platinum-resistant recurrent ovarian cancer
Guideline Action: Set treatment goals to improving quality of life by extending symptom-free interval, reducing symptom intensity, increasing progression-free interval, or prolonging life if possible.
Source Statement: Lower levels of response to treatment are expected for this group; therefore, the goals of treatment should be to improve patient's quality of life by extending the symptom-free interval, reducing symptom intensity, increasing progression-free interval, or if possible, prolonging life.

Rule ID: R007
Scenario: TREATMENT_RESPONSE
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: platinum-refractory or platinum-resistant recurrent ovarian cancer
Guideline Action: Use single-agent paclitaxel, topotecan, pegylated liposomal doxorubicin, or gemcitabine as reasonable treatment options.
Source Statement: Single-agent paclitaxel, topotecan, pegylated liposomal doxorubicin, and gemcitabine have demonstrated activity in this patient population and are reasonable treatment options.

Rule ID: R008
Scenario: TREATMENT_RESPONSE
Priority: 60
Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER
Activation Condition: platinum-sensitive recurrent ovarian cancer
Guideline Action: Offer chemotherapy with biologics after discussing the safety profile.
Source Statement: Women with platinum-sensitive recurrent ovarian cancer should be offered chemotherapy with biologics after a discussion concerning the safety profile

Priority: 80

rules_text:
Rule ID: R001
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 80
Recommendation Class: NOT_RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: heat exposure is prolonged or severe enough to cause body temperature above 38°C
Guideline Action: do not continue further exposures during the same day
Source Statement: There is abundant evidence that the physiological strain of an exposure which raises body temperature above 38°C is such as to contraindicate further exposures during the same day; it may take hours for complete recovery.

Rule ID: R002
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: employee exposure to heat in the workplace
Guideline Action: control heat exposure by requiring compliance with the work practice standard
Source Statement: NIOSH recommends that employee exposure to heat in the workplace be controlled by requiring compliance with the work practice standard set forth in the following sections.

Rule ID: R003
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: hot environmental conditions exceed WBGT 79°F
Guideline Action: apply the standard to all places of employment indoors and outdoors and to all employees except those required to wear impermeable protective clothing
Source Statement: The provisions of this standard are applicable to all places of employment, indoors and outdoors, and to all employees except those who are required to wear impermeable protective clothing.

Rule ID: R004
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: continuous exposure for one hour or intermittent exposure for two hours and WBGT exceeds 79°F for men or 76°F for women
Guideline Action: initiate one or a combination of the listed protective practices to keep body core temperature from exceeding 100.4°F
Source Statement: When exposure of an employee is continuous for one hour or intermittent for a period of two hours and the time-weighted average WBGT exceeds 79°F for men or 76°F for women, then any one or combination of the following practices shall be initiated to insure that the employee's body care temperature does not exceed 100.4°F:

Rule ID: R005
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: employee is unacclimatized
Guideline Action: acclimatize over 6 days starting at 50 percent of anticipated total work load and time exposure on day 1, then increase by 10 percent daily to 100 percent on day 6
Source Statement: Unacclimatized employees shall be acclimatized over a period of 6 days. The acclimatization schedule shall begin with 50 percent of the anticipated total work load and time exposure on the first day, followed by daily 10 percent increments building up 100 percent total exposure on the sixth day.

Rule ID: R006
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: regular acclimatized employee returns after nine or more consecutive calendar days of leave
Guideline Action: use a 4-day reacclimatization schedule starting at 50 percent on day 1 and increasing by 20 percent daily to 100 percent on day 4
Source Statement: Regular acclimatized employees who return from nine or more consecutive calendar days of leave, shall undergo a four day acclimatization period. The acclimatization schedule shall begin with 50 percent of the anticipated total exposure on the first day, followed by daily 20 percent increments building up to 100 percent total exposure on the fourth day.

Rule ID: R007
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: regular acclimatized employee returns after four consecutive days of illness
Guideline Action: obtain medical permission to return to work and use a 4-day reacclimatization schedule as above
Source Statement: Regular acclimatized employees who return from four consecutive days of illness should have medical permission to return to the job, and should undergo a four day re-acclimatization period as defined in (2) above.

Rule ID: R008
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: workers are exposed to hot jobs
Guideline Action: implement a work and rest regimen to reduce peaks of physiological strain and improve recovery during rest periods
Source Statement: A work and rest regimen shall be implemented to reduce the peaks of physiological strain and to improve recovery during rest periods.

Scenario: GENERAL

Source Statement: James et al. 2013 (ACT II), studied maintenance chemotherapy versus none following chemoradiation and found that maintenance chemotherapy does not improve overall survival or colostomy-free survival. rules_text:
Rule ID: R001
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: all patients with endometrial cancer after potentially curative primary treatment and no evidence of disease
Guideline Action: counsel about potential symptoms of recurrence
Source Statement: It is recommended that all patients receive counselling about the potential symptoms of recurrence of endometrial cancer, because the majority of recurrences in the identified studies were symptomatic.

Rule ID: R002
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: patient is surgically or pathologically confirmed low risk of recurrence (stage IA or IB, grade 1 or 2)
Guideline Action: perform general examination including complete history and pelvic-rectal examination semi-annually or annually for the first 3 years, then annually for the next 2 years
Source Statement: For patients at a surgically or pathologically confirmed low risk of recurrence (i.e., stage IA or IB, grade 1 or 2): A general examination, including a complete history and a pelvicrectal examination, conducted semi-annually or annually for the first three years and annually for the next two years.

Rule ID: R003
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: patient is high risk of recurrence (stage IA or IB, grade 3, or stage IC or advanced stage)
Guideline Action: perform general examination including complete history and pelvic-rectal examination every 3 to 6 months for the first 3 years, then semi-annually for the next 2 years
Source Statement: For patients at high risk of recurrence (i.e., stage IA or IB, grade 3, or stage IC or advanced stage). A general examination, including a complete history and a pelvic-rectal examination, every three to six months for the first three years and semi-annually for the next two years.

Rule ID: R004
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: planning follow-up setting or specialist type for any patient
Guideline Action: follow the patient with a health care professional knowledgeable about the natural history of the disease and comfortable performing speculum and pelvic exams
Source Statement: There is insufficient evidence to inform the optimum clinical setting or type of specialist required for follow-up; however, it is recommended that all patients be followed by a health care professional who is knowledgeable about the natural history of the disease, and who is comfortable performing speculum and pelvic exams, in order to diagnose or detect a local (vaginal) recurrence.

Rule ID: R005
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: patient has symptoms suggestive of recurrence
Guideline Action: perform targeted investigation to rule out recurrence
Source Statement: It is recommended that all patients undergo a targeted investigation to rule out recurrence if symptomatic, since patients with local recurrence are potentially curable with further therapy.

Rule ID: R006
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: treatment includes radiotherapy
Guideline Action: counsel the patient on potential adverse effects of radiotherapy
Source Statement: Where treatment with radiotherapy is involved, it is recommended that patients be counselled on the potential adverse effects of radiotherapy.

Rule ID: R007
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 60
Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER
Activation Condition: all patients with endometrial cancer after potentially curative primary treatment and no evidence of disease
Guideline Action: use a follow-up strategy based on recurrence risk and patient preferences
Source Statement: The most appropriate follow-up strategy is likely one based upon the risk of recurrence, with individual patient preferences for more or less follow-up taken into account.

Rule ID: R008
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 60
Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER
Activation Condition: patient has remained recurrence-free for 5 years
Guideline Action: return to annual population-based general physical and pelvic examination
Source Statement: Since the majority of patients with recurrence were symptomatic and virtually all recurred within five years, it seems reasonable that patients return to annual population-based general physical and pelvic examination after five years of recurrence-free follow-up.

patient_vignette: A 58-year-old woman with previously treated diffuse large B-cell lymphoma completed six cycles of R-CHOP eight months ago and achieved a complete metabolic response. She now returns for a routine follow-up visit without B symptoms, palpable adenopathy, or abnormal laboratory findings. Her oncologist notes that she feels well and asks whether she should have an FDG PET/CT scan to “make sure nothing is coming back.” There is no new clinical concern, and prior post-treatment imaging was reassuring. The main question is whether to continue scheduled surveillance imaging or use PET/CT as a routine monitoring test.

patient_vignette: A 14-year-old boy with localized Ewing’s sarcoma of the distal femur completed neoadjuvant chemotherapy and has had a marked radiographic and symptomatic response. Repeat MRI shows substantial shrinkage of the intramedullary and soft-tissue components, while the pre-chemotherapy MRI demonstrated more extensive marrow involvement. The orthopedic oncologist is planning limb-sparing surgery, but the post-treatment scan was obtained at an outside facility without the original pre-chemotherapy sequences for side-by-side comparison. The tumor board discusses local control with the patient and family, who want limb preservation if safe. Because the lesion appears smaller and resection seems feasible, the team is ready to finalize margins based on the new MRI alone. The bone lesion remains near the metaphysis, and the surgeons are cautious about preserving function while maintaining clearance.

Rule ID: R002
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 80
Recommendation Class: NOT_RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: positive sentinel node and comparing CLND with observation
Guideline Action: Do not expect benefit from CLND for any subgroup based on MSLT-II.

Rule ID: R003
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 80
Recommendation Class: NOT_RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: positive sentinel node and comparing CLND with observation
Guideline Action: Do not assume CLND improves distant metastasis-free survival, overall survival, or recurrence-free survival based on DeCOG-SLT.
Source Statement: The DeCOG-SLT trial found no difference in distant metastasis-free survival, overall survival, or recurrence-free survival when SLN positive patients who received CLND were compared to patients who were observed.

Rule ID: R004
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 80
Recommendation Class: NOT_RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: positive sentinel node and considering CLND versus observation
Guideline Action: Avoid routine CLND when observation with ultrasonography is feasible because CLND increases adverse events.

patient_vignette: A 25-year-old woman presents to discuss breast cancer screening. She was treated for Hodgkin lymphoma at age 18 with mantle radiation totaling 30 Gy, and her current risk assessment places her in risk category 4 because her family history is limited to a second-degree relative with breast cancer. She has no breast symptoms and is anxious because a relative was recently diagnosed with breast cancer. She asks whether she should begin screening now, since she has heard that high-risk women need early imaging. Her clinician reviews her history and confirms prior chest radiation, but notes that her risk category is not 5. The discussion focuses on what screening, if any, should be started at this age and whether MRI should be added to mammography later on.

rules_text:
Rule ID: R001
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 80
Recommendation Class: NOT_RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: woman is in risk category 5 and is age 25
Guideline Action: do not start screening from age 25
Source Statement: This (Ontario) Working Group, however, did not find justification for screening from age 25 in this group (or any of the other high risk groups).

Rule ID: R002
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: woman is in target population risk category 1, 2, 3, or 5
Guideline Action: perform MRI in addition to mammography
Source Statement: MRI in addition to mammography is recommended for women in target population risk categories 1, 2, 3, and 5 above.

Rule ID: R003
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 60
Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER
Activation Condition: women are being screened for high breast cancer risk
Guideline Action: screen annually
Source Statement: While there is insufficient evidence at this time to make a definitive recommendation regarding the appropriate screening frequency, it is the opinion of the Working Group that women should be screened annually, as this was the frequency typical of the identified studies on which the recommendation for screening is based.

Rule ID: R004
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 60
Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER
Activation Condition: women are being screened for high breast cancer risk
Guideline Action: screen from age 30 to 69 years
Source Statement: While there is insufficient evidence at this time to make a definitive recommendation regarding the ages of patients who should be screened, it is the opinion of the Working Group that women should be screened annually from 30 to 69 years of age.

Rule ID: R005
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 60
Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER
Activation Condition: woman is in risk category 5 and received at least 20 Gy radiation before age 30
Guideline Action: use MRI in addition to mammography because benefits outweigh harms
Source Statement: It is the opinion of the Working Group that the benefits of MRI in terms of increased sensitivity outweigh the potential harms of higher recall rates and biopsy rates for all women in risk category 5 who received ≥20 Gy radiation before the age of 30.

Rule ID: R006
Scenario: GENERAL

Guideline Action: consider adding MRI to mammography
Source Statement: With respect to risk category 4, there are preliminary data that a subgroup of patients in risk category 4 might benefit from the addition of MRI to mammography (e.g., women who in addition to a high risk benign biopsy or previous breast cancer, also have breast density ≥50% and a family history of breast cancer though insufficient to put them in category 3).

Recommendation Class: NO_RECOMMENDATION
Activation Condition: patient is in risk category 4
Guideline Action: do not make a recommendation for MRI screening based on current evidence
Source Statement: The evidence is insufficient to recommend MRI screening for patients in risk category 4.

Baseline labs show mild anemia and elevated LDH; renal and liver function are acceptable. The oncology team is planning first-line treatment and discusses CHOP-based chemotherapy. rules_text:
Rule ID: R001
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 60
Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER
Activation Condition: adult patient with relapsed SCLC
Guideline Action: Consider second-line chemotherapy only after weighing treatment-free interval, response to first-line therapy, residual toxicity, and performance status.
Source Statement: The selection of patients for treatment with second-line therapy should be dependent on the treatment-free interval, the extent of response to first-line therapy, residual toxicity from first-line therapy, and the performance status of the patient.

Rule ID: R002
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 60
Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER
Activation Condition: patient relapses three or more months after completion of first-line chemotherapy
Guideline Action: Consider retreatment with the same regimen that produced the initial response, generally etoposide-cisplatin.
Source Statement: patients who relapse three or more months following the completion of first-line chemotherapy may benefit from retreatment with the same regimen that induced their initial response. This would generally mean retreatment with etoposide-cisplatin.

Rule ID: R003
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 60
Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER
Activation Condition: patient relapses three or more months after completion of first-line chemotherapy
Guideline Action: Consider alternative regimens such as CAV or carboplatin plus etoposide.
Source Statement: Alternative regimens may include cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, and vincristine (CAV) or carboplatin and etoposide.

Rule ID: R004
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 60
Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER
Activation Condition: patient initially responded to chemotherapy and response duration was 45 days or longer
Guideline Action: Consider oral topotecan as an alternative second-line option.
Source Statement: Oral topotecan is a possible alternative for patients who initially responded to chemotherapy and had a response duration of 45 days or longer.

Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 60
Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER
Activation Condition: patient is not suitable for intravenous therapy and topotecan is being considered

Source Statement: Oral administration is more convenient and may be a treatment option for patients not suitable for intravenous therapy.

Priority: 60
Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER
Activation Condition: topotecan is given orally
Guideline Action: Monitor for grade 3/4 diarrhea.
Source Statement: Oral administration is associated with a higher incidence of grade 3/4 diarrhea, whereas intravenous administration may result in a higher frequency of grade 3/4 neutropenia.

Priority: 60
Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER

Rule ID: R001
Scenario: TREATMENT_RESPONSE
Priority: 80
Recommendation Class: NOT_RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: platinum-resistant recurrent ovarian cancer and not eligible for the AURELIA trial criteria
Guideline Action: Do not apply the bevacizumab plus chemotherapy option described for AURELIA-eligible patients.
Source Statement: Ineligible patients include those who have received >2 prior anticancer regimens or who had refractory disease, patients with a history of bowel obstruction (including subocclusive disease) related to underlying disease, a history of abdominal fistula, gastrointestinal perforation, or intra-abdominal abscess, or evidence of rectosigmoid involvement by pelvic examination, bowel involvement on computed tomography, or clinical symptoms of bowel obstruction.

Rule ID: R002
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: all patients with recurrent epithelial ovarian cancer
Guideline Action: Assess each patient individually for recurrence status, platinum sensitivity, toxicity, ease of administration, and patient preference; recognize systemic therapy is not curative.
Source Statement: Systemic therapy for recurrent ovarian cancer is not curative. As such, it is recognized that, to determine the optimal therapy, each patient needs to be assessed individually in terms of recurrence, sensitivity to platinum, toxicity, ease of administration, and patient preference.

Rule ID: R003
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: all patients with recurrent epithelial ovarian cancer
Guideline Action: Offer participation in clinical trials if appropriate.
Source Statement: All patients should be offered the opportunity to participate in clinical trials, if appropriate.

Rule ID: R004
Scenario: TREATMENT_RESPONSE
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: platinum-sensitive recurrent ovarian cancer and a single platinum agent is not being considered because of toxicity or allergy
Guideline Action: Use monotherapy with paclitaxel, topotecan, or pegylated liposomal doxorubicin.
Source Statement: If a single platinum agent is not being considered (e.g., because of toxicity or allergy), then monotherapy with paclitaxel, topotecan, or pegylated liposomal doxorubicin is a reasonable treatment option.

Rule ID: R005
Scenario: TREATMENT_RESPONSE
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: platinum-sensitive recurrent ovarian cancer with known BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation, somatic or germline, after platinum-based chemotherapy for recurrent disease
Guideline Action: Use PARP inhibitor maintenance treatment post platinum-based chemotherapy.
Source Statement: PARP inhibitors are recommended for patients with known BRCA 1 or 2 mutation (somatic and germline) as maintenance treatment post platinum-based chemotherapy for recurrent disease.

Rule ID: R006
Scenario: TREATMENT_RESPONSE
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: platinum-refractory or platinum-resistant recurrent ovarian cancer
Guideline Action: Set treatment goals to improving quality of life by extending symptom-free interval, reducing symptom intensity, increasing progression-free interval, or prolonging life if possible.
Source Statement: Lower levels of response to treatment are expected for this group; therefore, the goals of treatment should be to improve patient's quality of life by extending the symptom-free interval, reducing symptom intensity, increasing progression-free interval, or if possible, prolonging life.

Rule ID: R007

Priority: 70

Guideline Action: Use single-agent paclitaxel, topotecan, pegylated liposomal doxorubicin, or gemcitabine as reasonable treatment options.
Source Statement: Single-agent paclitaxel, topotecan, pegylated liposomal doxorubicin, and gemcitabine have demonstrated activity in this patient population and are reasonable treatment options.

Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 80

Activation Condition: Using a 37-mm plastic cassette for acrylamide sampling

Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED

Rule ID: R003
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: Collecting airborne acrylamide samples

Rule ID: R004
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: After collecting airborne acrylamide samples
Guideline Action: Extract acrylamide from the silica gel tube with methanol
Source Statement: The silica gel tube should then be treated with methanol to extract the acrylamide

Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70

Scenario: GENERAL

She is visibly anxious and says parents are “panicking” on social media, asking whether the school cafeteria food was contaminated and whether this could be a deliberate poisoning. Priority: 80

Guideline Action: Do not discuss liability, blame, or cause before the situation is contained.
Source Statement: Avoid discussing liability: Questions of cause, blame, responsibility, and liability often follow a crisis. It is not appropriate to discuss them at the early stages.

Guideline Action: Do not speculate about bioterrorism; refer questions to law enforcement and coordinate statements.

patient_vignette: A 29-year-old warehouse worker presents to occupational health after a late-afternoon shift in a non-air-conditioned loading dock. He had been stacking boxes and moving pallets for about 90 minutes with only brief water breaks. On the site nurse’s check, his oral temperature is 38.4°C, and he reports marked fatigue, heavy sweating, and a throbbing headache. He says he feels better after resting indoors for 20 minutes, but the supervisor wants him to return to the dock to finish the shift. He is otherwise healthy and has no history of heat illness. The workplace had been unusually hot all day, and several coworkers were also complaining of the heat.

rules_text:
Rule ID: R001
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 80
Recommendation Class: NOT_RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: heat exposure is prolonged or severe enough to cause body temperature above 38°C
Guideline Action: do not continue further exposures during the same day
Source Statement: There is abundant evidence that the physiological strain of an exposure which raises body temperature above 38°C is such as to contraindicate further exposures during the same day; it may take hours for complete recovery.

Rule ID: R002
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: employee exposure to heat in the workplace
Guideline Action: control heat exposure by requiring compliance with the work practice standard
Source Statement: NIOSH recommends that employee exposure to heat in the workplace be controlled by requiring compliance with the work practice standard set forth in the following sections.

Rule ID: R003
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: hot environmental conditions exceed WBGT 79°F
Guideline Action: apply the standard to all places of employment indoors and outdoors and to all employees except those required to wear impermeable protective clothing
Source Statement: The provisions of this standard are applicable to all places of employment, indoors and outdoors, and to all employees except those who are required to wear impermeable protective clothing.

Rule ID: R004
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: continuous exposure for one hour or intermittent exposure for two hours and WBGT exceeds 79°F for men or 76°F for women
Guideline Action: initiate one or a combination of the listed protective practices to keep body core temperature from exceeding 100.4°F
Source Statement: When exposure of an employee is continuous for one hour or intermittent for a period of two hours and the time-weighted average WBGT exceeds 79°F for men or 76°F for women, then any one or combination of the following practices shall be initiated to insure that the employee's body care temperature does not exceed 100.4°F:

Rule ID: R005
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: employee is unacclimatized
Guideline Action: acclimatize over 6 days starting at 50 percent of anticipated total work load and time exposure on day 1, then increase by 10 percent daily to 100 percent on day 6
Source Statement: Unacclimatized employees shall be acclimatized over a period of 6 days. The acclimatization schedule shall begin with 50 percent of the anticipated total work load and time exposure on the first day, followed by daily 10 percent increments building up 100 percent total exposure on the sixth day.

Rule ID: R006
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: regular acclimatized employee returns after nine or more consecutive calendar days of leave
Guideline Action: use a 4-day reacclimatization schedule starting at 50 percent on day 1 and increasing by 20 percent daily to 100 percent on day 4
Source Statement: Regular acclimatized employees who return from nine or more consecutive calendar days of leave, shall undergo a four day acclimatization period. The acclimatization schedule shall begin with 50 percent of the anticipated total exposure on the first day, followed by daily 20 percent increments building up to 100 percent total exposure on the fourth day.

Rule ID: R007
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: regular acclimatized employee returns after four consecutive days of illness
Guideline Action: obtain medical permission to return to work and use a 4-day reacclimatization schedule as above
Source Statement: Regular acclimatized employees who return from four consecutive days of illness should have medical permission to return to the job, and should undergo a four day re-acclimatization period as defined in (2) above.

Rule ID: R008
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: workers are exposed to hot jobs
Guideline Action: implement a work and rest regimen to reduce peaks of physiological strain and improve recovery during rest periods
Source Statement: A work and rest regimen shall be implemented to reduce the peaks of physiological strain and to improve recovery during rest periods.

Scenario: GENERAL

Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70

Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: person is traveling to or working in a country with high or intermediate hepatitis A endemicity and is susceptible
Guideline Action: Vaccinate before departure or give immune globulin before departure; vaccine is preferred.
Source Statement: All susceptible persons traveling to or working in countries that have high or intermediate hepatitis A endemicity (Figure 4) should be vaccinated or receive IG before departure (Tables 1-4). Hepatitis A vaccination at the age-appropriate dose is preferred (Tables 2-4).

Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: traveler departs in less than 4 weeks and cannot or will not receive immune globulin
Guideline Action: Still give hepatitis A vaccine and inform the traveler protection may be incomplete for the next 2-4 weeks.
Source Statement: Travelers departing in <4 weeks who do not or cannot receive IG should nonetheless receive hepatitis A vaccine and be informed that they might not be optimally protected from acquiring hepatitis A in the immediate future (i.e., subsequent 2-4 weeks).

Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70

Travelers whose travel period is >2 months should be administered IG at 0.06 mL/kg; administration must be repeated if the travel period is >5 months (Table 1).

patient_vignette: A 59-year-old man presents with a firm, painless left level II cervical lymph node that has enlarged over 6 weeks. He has no dysphagia, odynophagia, otalgia, weight loss, or visible mucosal lesion on careful head and neck examination. Flexible nasopharyngolaryngoscopy is unrevealing, and contrast-enhanced CT of the neck does not identify a clear primary tumor. The neck mass is easily palpable and accessible for physical examination and biopsy. The clinician is considering PET/CT to look for nodal disease and to help localize a primary site before panendoscopy.

Source Statement: For patients with stage IIIA, IIIB, IIIC, IIID, or resected IV melanoma: 3.1 Clinical follow-up with history and physical examination with full skin and lymph node examination by a dermatologist (with photo-surveillance and dermoscopy if indicated), and/or a surgeon, medical oncologist, or cancer nurse specialist should occur every three to six months in years 1 to 3, then every six months in years 4 to 5, or as clinically indicated.

reference_actions: ["Counsel the patient about potential symptoms of recurrence of endometrial cancer.", "Arrange general examination, including complete history and pelvic-rectal examination, semi-annually or annually for the first 3 years, then annually for the next 2 years, because she is low risk of recurrence.", "Follow her with a health care professional knowledgeable about the natural history of the disease and comfortable performing speculum and pelvic exams.", "Use a follow-up strategy based on recurrence risk and the patient\u2019s preferences."]
rules_text:
Rule ID: R001
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: all patients with endometrial cancer after potentially curative primary treatment and no evidence of disease
Guideline Action: counsel about potential symptoms of recurrence
Source Statement: It is recommended that all patients receive counselling about the potential symptoms of recurrence of endometrial cancer, because the majority of recurrences in the identified studies were symptomatic.

Rule ID: R002
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: patient is surgically or pathologically confirmed low risk of recurrence (stage IA or IB, grade 1 or 2)
Guideline Action: perform general examination including complete history and pelvic-rectal examination semi-annually or annually for the first 3 years, then annually for the next 2 years
Source Statement: For patients at a surgically or pathologically confirmed low risk of recurrence (i.e., stage IA or IB, grade 1 or 2): A general examination, including a complete history and a pelvicrectal examination, conducted semi-annually or annually for the first three years and annually for the next two years.

Rule ID: R003
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: patient is high risk of recurrence (stage IA or IB, grade 3, or stage IC or advanced stage)
Guideline Action: perform general examination including complete history and pelvic-rectal examination every 3 to 6 months for the first 3 years, then semi-annually for the next 2 years
Source Statement: For patients at high risk of recurrence (i.e., stage IA or IB, grade 3, or stage IC or advanced stage). A general examination, including a complete history and a pelvic-rectal examination, every three to six months for the first three years and semi-annually for the next two years.

Rule ID: R004
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: planning follow-up setting or specialist type for any patient
Guideline Action: follow the patient with a health care professional knowledgeable about the natural history of the disease and comfortable performing speculum and pelvic exams
Source Statement: There is insufficient evidence to inform the optimum clinical setting or type of specialist required for follow-up; however, it is recommended that all patients be followed by a health care professional who is knowledgeable about the natural history of the disease, and who is comfortable performing speculum and pelvic exams, in order to diagnose or detect a local (vaginal) recurrence.

Rule ID: R005
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: patient has symptoms suggestive of recurrence
Guideline Action: perform targeted investigation to rule out recurrence
Source Statement: It is recommended that all patients undergo a targeted investigation to rule out recurrence if symptomatic, since patients with local recurrence are potentially curable with further therapy.

Rule ID: R006
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: treatment includes radiotherapy
Guideline Action: counsel the patient on potential adverse effects of radiotherapy
Source Statement: Where treatment with radiotherapy is involved, it is recommended that patients be counselled on the potential adverse effects of radiotherapy.

Rule ID: R007
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 60
Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER
Activation Condition: all patients with endometrial cancer after potentially curative primary treatment and no evidence of disease
Guideline Action: use a follow-up strategy based on recurrence risk and patient preferences
Source Statement: The most appropriate follow-up strategy is likely one based upon the risk of recurrence, with individual patient preferences for more or less follow-up taken into account.

Rule ID: R008
Scenario: GENERAL
Priority: 60
Recommendation Class: CONDITIONAL_CONSIDER
Activation Condition: patient has remained recurrence-free for 5 years
Guideline Action: return to annual population-based general physical and pelvic examination
Source Statement: Since the majority of patients with recurrence were symptomatic and virtually all recurred within five years, it seems reasonable that patients return to annual population-based general physical and pelvic examination after five years of recurrence-free follow-up.

patient_vignette: A 62-year-old man is diagnosed with stage III squamous cell carcinoma of the oropharynx after biopsy of a persistent throat lesion and CT imaging showing a primary tumor with suspicious cervical nodes. He is referred to a multidisciplinary head and neck cancer clinic where the medical oncologist, radiation oncologist, head and neck surgeon, speech-language pathologist, dietitian, and social worker review his case together. The team discusses definitive treatment planning, swallowing rehabilitation, nutritional support, and survivorship needs. His family physician is informed of the diagnosis and remains responsible for his general medical care and supportive follow-up after cancer treatment. Because he may need surgery depending on response to therapy, the surgeon notes that reconstruction expertise would be required if an operation becomes necessary.

patient_vignette: A 58-year-old woman is diagnosed with ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) after a screening mammogram showed clustered microcalcifications in the upper outer quadrant of the left breast. Core biopsy confirms intermediate-grade DCIS. Breast imaging shows a 2.1 cm localized area without multifocal disease, and the breast surgeon feels she is a good candidate for breast-conserving surgery. The patient is anxious about recurrence but strongly prefers to preserve her breast if oncologically appropriate. She asks about treatment options and whether radiation would still be needed after surgery.

Scenario: INITIAL_DIAGNOSIS
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: woman has DCIS and is a candidate for breast-conserving surgery
Guideline Action: offer choice of breast-conserving surgery or total mastectomy
Source Statement: Women with DCIS of the breast who are candidates for breast-conserving surgery should be offered the choice of breast-conserving surgery or total mastectomy.

Rule ID: R002
Scenario: INITIAL_DIAGNOSIS
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: breast-conserving surgery is performed for DCIS
Guideline Action: remove all mammographically suspicious calcifications and ensure microscopically clear margins of DCIS

Rule ID: R003
Scenario: INITIAL_DIAGNOSIS
Priority: 70
Recommendation Class: RECOMMENDED
Activation Condition: DCIS is large enough that breast-conserving surgery would leave an unacceptable cosmetic result
Guideline Action: recommend mastectomy with option of reconstruction
